I’ll trace the broadcast lifecycle and its schedule API, then make the smallest change that restores a live scheduled broadcast to draft and ensures each launch creates an active schedule. I’ll avoid installing dependencies or running the test suite as requested.
This touches the Broadcasts frontend workflow, so I’m following the repository’s frontend component conventions before editing the lifecycle controls.
The existing launch flow creates another schedule but leaves an older paused one in place. I’ll make the launch path remove all existing schedules while the broadcast is still draft, then activate it and create exactly one new schedule. I’ll also add an explicit “Edit broadcast” action only for scheduled broadcasts that have not started sending.
Implemented the Broadcasts lifecycle change.

- Added an **Edit broadcast** action for active scheduled broadcasts that have not begun sending. It moves the broadcast back to draft and opens it for editing.
- On launch, existing schedules are deleted before activation; a scheduled launch then creates one fresh active schedule. This prevents relaunches from retaining a paused schedule or accumulating stale schedules.
- The edit action is hidden while batch-job status is loading and for broadcasts that already have runs.
